bull_bear.body:
- Dominant ~40%+ revenue share of the Indian Satcom market, reinforcing its leadership position
- Incumbency advantage: long-standing partnerships and a strong customer base provide a distinct competitive moat as the industry moves to a multi-player, multi-orbit ecosystem
- Multi-technology / multi-constellation (GEO-LEO) partnership model that lets it adopt the Satcom technology best suited to each customer application
- Gateway, teleport and network redundancy infrastructure supporting the very high uptime required by mission-critical customers
- Strong traction and incremental growth in Maritime and Aero in-flight connectivity verticals, plus a deepened Government footprint
- Wholly owned subsidiary Nelco Network Products Ltd. and associate Piscis Networks Pvt. Ltd. extending the equipment and networking offering
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Regulatory and policy dependence - LEO / spectrum authorisations — India's Satcom sector is undergoing rapid policy evolution with ongoing discussions on spectrum assignment, usage charges and new authorizations. Management states the commercial ramp-up of LEO services is pending regulatory approvals and that this delay is directly impacting growth across multiple segments, deferring hybrid GEO-LEO deployments and associated equipment sales. The Company mitigates through continuous engagement with regulators and industry associations to ensure market access.
- Critical satellite and ground infrastructure failure — Operations depend on critical physical and satellite infrastructure susceptible to natural disasters, power outages, cyber incidents or human error; an unforeseen satellite failure could affect service continuity until alternative transponder capacity is available. Resilience is built through access to multiple satellites, teleport redundancy and hybrid networks. The BRSR materiality table repeats this as a business-continuity risk carrying revenue loss, recovery cost and brand damage.
- Supply chain and geopolitical exposure to imported Satcom hardware — The ongoing conflict in the Middle East has introduced fresh volatility into global logistics and component sourcing; while semiconductor shortages have eased, geopolitical tensions threaten the stability of critical electronics and specialised Satcom hardware - particularly critical given the sector's reliance on imported Satcom equipment. Management also flags that input costs are rising due to the geopolitical situation, exerting further pressure on margins. Mitigation is via strategic partnerships, diversified sourcing, inventory planning and strategic buffer stocks.
- Intensifying competition from global entrants — The entry of global players into the Indian market alongside established domestic entities is intensifying competition, in a business where the Company currently holds a dominant ~40%+ revenue share it must defend. The Company responds by exploring new use cases, markets and strategic partnerships.
- Technology obsolescence and migration cost — Rapid evolution in Satcom technologies creates challenges of adoption and obsolescence; the AR explicitly states that migration to newer systems involves cost and transitional complexity which may temporarily impact margins. Mitigated by investment in scalable, interoperable systems and long-term OEM partnerships.
- Demand volatility and vertical concentration — Demand for satellite services is influenced by macroeconomic trends, availability of alternate technologies, government spending and sectoral shifts, and fluctuations in key verticals could affect short-term revenue and profitability. The AR also notes select segments are undergoing natural lifecycle contractions and that legacy equipment revenue streams are stagnant or declining; the Company is developing new segments to reduce dependency on a few markets.
- Cybersecurity and data privacy — As a satellite communication operator, data breaches and cyber-attacks could expose the Company to significant financial and reputational loss. Controls cited include ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification, periodic VAPT and security audits, real-time threat monitoring, role-based access and encryption, third-party/vendor security assessment, and an FY2025-26 expansion of the internal audit scope to cover cybersecurity and cyber-financial risks. The Company states it has reinforced its resilience framework with advanced encryption and redundant network paths to ensure 99.9% uptime.
- Foreign currency exposure and offshore revenue concentration — Forex exposures are monitored through board-approved hedging strategies with net positions kept within defined risk thresholds - structurally relevant because BRSR Section A reports 31.05% of turnover as revenue generated by providing services to customers located outside India, alongside imported equipment sourcing.

business.body: Nelco operates in a single reportable segment, Network Systems, comprising Satellite Communication (Satcom) services along with related equipment sales, maintenance and other allied services. It delivers managed satellite connectivity, gateway/teleport and network infrastructure and application-specific solutions to Enterprise, Government, Defense, Maritime and Aero (in-flight connectivity) customers across India, including remote and under-connected geographies. The Company is enhancing its role from being only a Satcom connectivity provider to becoming an integrated solution provider, building hybrid multi-orbit GEO-LEO offerings through multi-technology partnerships.

business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Shift from being only a Satcom connectivity provider to an integrated solution provider, anchored on four pillars: market expansion, infrastructure leadership, strategic partnerships and innovation leadership.
- Accelerated roll-out of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite services once commercially available, so as to offer resilient multi-orbit GEO-LEO services as a clear market differentiator.
- Solution-led growth: expand application-specific offerings across sectors, offering managed services and solutions alongside multi-orbit GEO-LEO hybrid connectivity.
- Infrastructure resilience: strengthen gateway, teleport and network redundancy capabilities to support multi-orbit (GSO & NGSO) operations and deliver the very high uptime mission-critical customers require.
- Partnership enablement: deepen collaboration with global satellite operators (existing and new LEO entrants), technology providers and domestic ecosystem partners, including multi-constellation GEO/LEO access.
- Operational excellence: automated network monitoring, AI-driven fault prediction and customer portal upgrades to raise service delivery and overall efficiency.
- Future readiness: prepare networks and systems for multi-orbit and next-generation service models.
- Policy advocacy: proactively engage regulators and government bodies on spectrum allocation, licensing frameworks and security norms.
- Talent and culture: upskill teams on next-gen Satcom technologies, data analytics and customer solutioning while embedding the IMPACT values.
- Reliability, security and sector-specific application mapping - tailoring Satcom technologies to Enterprise, Government, Defense, Maritime and Aero segments.
- Disciplined capital allocation - invest in infrastructure, partnerships and capabilities that offer sustainable returns and strategic relevance; continuously evaluate augmentation of technology, satellite network capability and ground infrastructure.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Nelco discloses no named plant, capacity-addition or commissioning project; its expansion is network- and infrastructure-led rather than manufacturing capex. The Directors' Report states that the Company continuously evaluates opportunities for investment and augmentation of its technology, satellite network capabilities and ground infrastructure, and for developing new products and services to enable ubiquitous, reliable, secure and high-quality Satcom connectivity. Under its FY2026-27 strategic priorities the Company intends to strengthen gateway, teleport and network redundancy capabilities so as to support multi-orbit (GSO and NGSO) operations and deliver the very high uptime required by mission-critical customers, and to prepare networks and systems for multi-orbit and next-generation service models (Future Readiness). Capital allocation is described as disciplined - investing in infrastructure, partnerships and capabilities that offer sustainable returns and strategic relevance - and the MD notes the Company is investing in advanced technologies and building newer solutions. The single largest expansion lever is the accelerated roll-out of LEO services and hybrid GEO-LEO offerings, which remain pending regulatory approvals in India; no rupee quantum, timeline or named project is attached to any of these. The Board also confirmed that no material changes and commitments occurred after the close of the year that affect the financial position of the Company.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- LEO commercial ramp-up is the pivotal catalyst: the delay in regulatory approvals has tempered near-term revenue growth as the expected market expansion did not happen, and customers increasingly expect hybrid GEO-LEO offerings that are not yet commercially deployable.
- Portfolio in transition - accelerated growth in emerging segments is progressively offsetting structural declines in some traditional verticals, while select segments undergo natural lifecycle contractions that dampen near-term growth.
- Management expects momentum to build as new segments scale and regulatory clearances are granted, returning the Company to a sustained growth trajectory in the coming years; investments already made in new segments are expected to start generating accelerated revenue.
- Input costs are rising due to the prevailing geopolitical situation, exerting further pressure on margins.
- India as the fastest-growing large economy at ~6.5% GDP growth, with Union Budget 2026-27 shifting from connectivity expansion to 'service depth' and state governments defining their own space policies, creating localized funded infrastructure pipelines.
- Union Budget 2026-27 demand drivers: a 38% increase in Telecom outlay to Rs 73,990 crore plus Space Mission 2.0 and the RISE framework; tax incentives for AI-driven data centres needing low-latency links; a record Rs 7.85 lakh crore Defence budget with a 22 percent rise in capital expenditure; maritime and energy security allocations; and education/healthcare digital initiatives.
- Structural shift globally to a 'security-first' model - geopolitical fragmentation drives demand for sovereign, resilient networks and sustained increases in Defense spending, with Satcom moving from a niche alternative to a foundational layer of digital architecture.
- Industry structure moving to multi-orbit architectures (GEO complemented by LEO), hybrid satellite-terrestrial networks as the new standard, a definitive shift from standalone bandwidth sales to managed services, more global operators entering India, and rising emphasis on security, redundancy and low-latency use cases.
- Incumbency moat: for players like Nelco, long-standing partnerships and a strong customer base provide a distinct competitive moat as the industry evolves into a dynamic, multi-player, multi-orbit ecosystem; offset by rapid technological shifts and intensifying competition as global players enter the domestic market.
- Opportunity clusters cited: bridging the digital divide / satellite backhaul for 4G-5G, mobility (in-flight connectivity, maritime, connected fleets), Defense and strategic autonomy under Atmanirbhar Bharat, satellite IoT and remote monitoring, disaster preparedness, smart cities and utilities backhaul, and telemedicine / remote education.
- Segment-level traction in FY26: strong incremental growth in Maritime and Aero in-flight connectivity, and a deepened Government footprint with an expanded share of new business, against stagnant or faster-declining legacy equipment revenue streams (notably at subsidiary NNPL).
